questions.prompt: Which GitHub profile is most likely to impress for a junior backend role?
options: One finished payments API with tests, CI and a clear README
Fifteen tutorial copies with no READMEs
One huge repo with a single commit called "final"
An empty profile with a great photo
questions.explanation: Finished, tested and explained beats lots of half-done work.

questions.prompt: What's the most valuable thing to include in your README's "design decisions"?
options: Why you made each choice, e.g. why amounts are in pence
The full text of PCI DSS
questions.explanation: Explaining *why* shows understanding, which is exactly what interviewers probe.

questions.prompt: Put the terminal steps for publishing a new project in order.
questions.explanation: Create the repo locally, stage, commit, connect to GitHub, push.

questions.prompt: You don't understand part of the starter code. What should you do before an interview?
options: Learn it until you can explain it, or replace it with something you can
Leave it and hope they don't ask
questions.explanation: Interviewers often pick a line and ask why it's there. Own every line.
